issues.body: `_policy_derived_output_keys()` collects every `Assign` with `ast.walk()` and only ever adds names to `tainted`; it does not respect statement order, control flow, or assignments that kill prior taint. For example, a resolver containing `repos = load(open("policy/repos.toml", "rb"))` followed by `repos = ["some-owner/some-name"]` and `print("repos=" + json.dumps(repos))` is reported as policy-derived. The same false positive occurs when the policy assignment is under `if False:` before a live hardcoded assignment. Thus a valid workflow mutation can publish a copied enabled set while the shipped assertion and current decoy mutant remain green. This is the prior policy-sourcing finding narrowed to the new analyzer, not a completed proof of executable dataflow.
issues.fix_hint: Make the analysis order- and control-flow-aware enough to prove the value reaching the `repos=` print is derived on live paths, including killing taint on hardcoded reassignment and rejecting unreachable seeds. At minimum, add non-crashing overwrite-after-policy and dead-branch-policy mutants whose named `resolve_policy_derived_outputs` finding becomes empty while the full self-test row count is preserved.
issues.title: Policy taint survives overwrites and unreachable assignments

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The prior resolver job/step conditionality finding is fixed: both seams are now reported by presence and exact value, with deleted and inert mutants. The policy-source check is materially stronger than the prior cross-step substring, but it still accepts a hardcoded resolver when a policy-derived assignment is overwritten or lies in unreachable code. Because the marquee one-source-of-truth assertion can still stay green after the live output is severed from policy, one major finding remains.
